issues.sym: On early cars a wheel could feel loose, wobble or make clunking noises, and in the worst case come off the car, sometimes after only a few hundred miles.
issues.why: The bolts that hold the hub to the car could work loose from repeated hard turning and braking. Toyota first told owners not to drive the cars at all until a fix was ready.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. Dealers replace the hub bolts (and the wheels where needed) for free. If a wheel ever feels loose or noisy, stop and have it towed.

issues.t: 12-volt battery goes dead, car won't start or unlock
issues.sym: After sitting for a day or two the car is completely dead: the key fob won't unlock it, the screens stay dark, and it won't go into Ready mode. Some owners see a 'parking brake cannot be applied' message. A jump start often brings it back, until the next time.
issues.why: Like every EV, the bZ4X uses a small 12-volt battery to wake up its computers and switch on the main battery. Owners report that it drains while parked and isn't always topped up from the big battery. A class action filed in 2025 claims replacement batteries fail as well.
issues.next: Keep a small jump pack in the car and use the mechanical key in the fob to get in. Have the dealer test the 12-volt battery and charging system, check for software updates, and keep records of every visit in case the problem keeps coming back.

issues.t: Defroster and heat stop working from A/C compressor fault (recall)
issues.sym: The windshield fogs up and the defroster blows cold or weak air, or the A/C and heat stop working. Some owners hear a grinding noise from the compressor first.
issues.why: The bZ4X heats and cools the cabin with an electric compressor. When that compressor or another part of the system fails, the climate software could shut the defroster off along with it, so the glass can't be cleared.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. Dealers update the climate control software and inspect the electric compressor, replacing it for free if needed. Parts have been on back order, so ask the dealer about a loaner if the defroster doesn't work.

issues.t: Rearview camera freezes or goes blank (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the backup camera picture freezes or the screen stays blank.
issues.why: A software error in the parking camera system (Panoramic View Monitor) can stop the camera image from showing.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN and have the dealer install the free parking-assist software update. Until then, use your mirrors and look over your shoulder when backing up.

issues.t: DC fast charging slows sharply after repeated sessions
issues.sym: On a road trip the first one or two fast-charging stops are normal, but after that charging crawls along at a fraction of the usual speed, so stops take much longer than expected.
issues.why: Early 2023 cars limited fast-charging speed to protect the battery once a lot of energy had been added in one day, and charged slowly when the battery was cold. Toyota released software updates to improve fast-charging speed on 2023 models.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer whether the charging software updates (bulletins 22TC11 and 23TC05) have been done on your car. On long trips, plan extra time and use Level 2 charging overnight where you can.

issues.t: Very slow fast charging in cold weather
issues.sym: In winter, DC fast charging is much slower than advertised, and in very cold weather the car may barely charge at a fast charger at all.
issues.why: A cold battery can't safely take a fast charge, so the car slows charging until the battery warms up. Toyota says charging time grows a lot below about 50°F, more so on AWD models, and charging may not work around -4°F. For 2024 Toyota added hardware to warm the battery better.
issues.next: Drive for a while before fast charging so the battery is warm, and charge at home when you can. If charging is slow even in mild weather, have the dealer check for software updates and run a charging-system check.

issues.t: Big range drop in freezing weather
issues.sym: In winter the estimated range falls well below the window sticker, sometimes by more than a third.
issues.why: Cold slows the chemistry inside the battery, and heating the cabin and the battery uses a lot of energy. In a Canadian winter test a bZ4X went about 37% less far than its official range.
issues.next: This is normal EV behavior, not a defect. Preheat the car while it is still plugged in, use the heated seats and steering wheel instead of high cabin heat, and leave a bigger range buffer on winter trips.

issues.t: Sudden loss of power or electrical shutdown while driving
issues.sym: While driving, the dash lights flicker or go out, warning messages appear, the car shakes or feels like it is shutting off, or a drive motor stops working.
issues.why: Owners have reported these events to NHTSA. Causes vary; one report was a failed front drive motor. A low or failing 12-volt battery can also make the electronics act up.
issues.next: If it happens, steer to a safe place and turn on the hazards. Have the car towed to a dealer, ask them to save any fault codes, and check for open recalls or software updates. These repairs should be covered by the EV warranty.

issues.t: Wheel-well liners or underbody cover torn loose
issues.sym: A flapping, scraping or rubbing noise after driving through deep water or puddles. Plastic wheel-well liners can be pulled into the tires, and the front bumper or underbody cover can come loose.
issues.why: Owners report that water hitting the plastic underbody panels at speed can rip them from their clips. Once loose, the panels drag on the road or rub the tires.
issues.next: Pull over and look under the car if you hear scraping. Have loose liners or covers reattached or replaced with new clips before they catch a tire. Slow down through standing water.

issues.t: Uneven or fast tire wear and vibration
issues.sym: Tires wear faster than expected or unevenly on the edges, or the car shakes above about 50 mph.
issues.why: EVs are heavy and have instant torque, which is hard on tires. Owners also report wear from alignment that is out of spec, and one owner traced a vibration to a foam noise pad inside the tire coming loose.
issues.next: Rotate the tires every 5,000 miles, check pressures monthly and get an alignment check if wear is uneven. A shop can balance or inspect the tire if you feel a vibration.

issues.t: Knocking from the rear over rough roads
issues.sym: A knocking or clunking from the rear wheels when driving slowly over bumps or rough pavement, which may get worse over time.
issues.why: Owners have reported this to NHTSA, and in those reports dealer visits did not fix it. The exact cause has not been confirmed.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension checked under warranty. Describe when it happens, try to record the sound, and ask the dealer to test drive it with you on a rough road.

issues.t: Wrong load capacity label with dealer accessories (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you can feel. The tire and loading sticker on the door jamb may list the wrong weight for accessories installed by the distributor.
issues.why: On some cars fitted with Gulf States Toyota accessories, the label didn't correctly account for their added weight, which could lead an owner to overload the car.
issues.next: Check the recall with your VIN. A corrected label is mailed out for free; stick it over the old one.
